prompt: Two classes both average 75, but one has scores from 40 to 100 and the other from 70 to 80.
tells: one has scores from 40 to 100 and the other from 70 to 80
why: Both classes average 75, but one is spread from 40 to 100 and the other from 70 to 80. Standard deviation measures that spread.
trap: The averages match; the spread doesn't.

prompt: A factory checks how far bolt lengths typically stray from the target.
tells: how far bolt lengths typically stray
why: How far lengths typically stray from the target is a measure of spread. Standard deviation is the typical distance from the center.
trap: It isn't about one bad bolt.

prompt: An investor says one fund's returns swing much more from year to year.
tells: swing much more from year to year
why: Returns that swing more from year to year are more spread out around their average. Investors call that volatility, which is standard deviation.
trap: Nothing is moving with anything else.

prompt: Most heights in the group fall within a few centimeters of the average.
tells: within a few centimeters of the average
why: Most heights fall within a few centimeters of the average, so the values are tightly packed. That's a small standard deviation.
trap: It describes the spread around the average, not the average.

prompt: A delivery company wants arrival times that are not just good on average but consistent.
tells: not just good on average but consistent
why: Good on average isn't enough if some deliveries are very late. Consistency means a low spread, which is a small standard deviation.

prompt: Error bars on a chart show how spread out the measurements were.
tells: how spread out the measurements were
why: Error bars show how far the measurements were spread around each value. They usually show the standard deviation or a range built from it.
trap: They don't mark a single odd point.
